name: install-mode-registry
purpose: Separates installation profiles for people who only want to use the platform from developer installations for improving the platform itself.

reader_guide.summary: Use this registry before setting up the workspace. Pick user mode for running or viewing platform outputs; pick developer mode for changing platform code, rules, tools, tests, or configs.
how_to_read: Read mode_boundary first so work_mode and install_mode are not confused.
Read modes to choose user or developer installation.
Use commands as planned setup commands, not as proof that installation occurred.
If a command is actually run and changes dependency or environment state, follow the installation audit workflow.
update_triggers: A developer improvement install path changes.
A package manager, dependency manifest, lock file, or runtime setup changes.
The platform adds a new root project with installable runtime dependencies.

structure_rules.rule: install_mode selects the environment setup profile; work_mode still controls planning, evidence, evaluation, and close-out strictness.
structure_rules.reason: The repository already has work modes. Installation audience should not weaken governance requirements.

structure_rules.rule: User installation should prefer regular installs, existing built artifacts, read-only viewing, and minimal runtime dependencies. It should not require editable installs or platform test harnesses.
structure_rules.reason: A person using the platform should not need the full improvement toolchain.

structure_rules.rule: Developer installation should use editable/local project setup where applicable and include tests, audits, and generated navigation checks.
structure_rules.reason: People improving the platform need fast code iteration and stronger verification.

structure_rules.rule: Commands in this registry are planned setup commands. If an agent actually runs an install, upgrade, removal, or global configuration, it must create an installation audit record.
structure_rules.reason: The registry describes how to set up. The installation registry records what actually changed.

field_guide.meaning: Explains the difference between install_mode and work_mode.
Fallback install mode when the user does not specify an installation audience.
Stable install mode identifier, currently user or developer.
Concrete setup commands grouped by project and purpose.
Checks to run after the installation profile is applied.

mode_boundary.install_mode: Environment setup profile for a human or agent preparing to use or improve the platform.
mode_boundary.work_mode: Task execution and close-out strictness profile such as quick, standard, ship_first, research, or governance.
mode_boundary.rule: Choose install_mode when setting up dependencies or runtime environment. Choose work_mode for each task after web-first intake and memory bootstrap.

modes.label: User Install
modes.intent: Use the platform, view generated artifacts, run the monitoring site, or execute stable CLI behavior without changing platform internals.
audience: reviewer viewing history, docs, dashboards, or generated artifacts
future public user trying the repository without improving it
dependency_policy: Prefer regular Python local installs over editable installs.
Prefer existing HTML/static artifacts when no runtime is needed.
For Next.js source builds, install from lock files and run the build; for runtime-only deployment, omit dev dependencies only after the build path is confirmed.
Do not install browser validation harnesses or governance test toolchains unless the user explicitly switches to developer install.
allowed_actions: build or run workspace-monitor for browsing repository state
must_not: edit platform source as part of setup
run editable Python installs by default
treat user setup as permission to change dependencies
skip installation audit if setup commands are actually executed

commands.purpose: Install the Python platform CLI in regular local mode.
commands.command: cd agent-platform && python3 -m venv .venv && . .venv/bin/activate && python -m pip install .
commands.notes: Regular install mirrors package installation more closely than editable install.

commands.purpose: Build the repository monitoring site from source for local viewing or Vercel readiness.
commands.command: cd workspace-monitor && npm ci && npm run build
commands.notes: Next.js source builds may need devDependencies during build; production runtime pruning is separate from build setup.

commands.purpose: View generated HTML presentation artifacts without installing the browser test harness.
commands.notes: Use developer install only when validating or modifying deck-generation/browser-test tooling.

verification: agent-platform: agent-platform --help or PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m agent_platform.cli list-agents
workspace-monitor: npm run build completes or Vercel build succeeds
presentation-agent: target HTML artifact opens in a browser

modes.label: Developer Improvement Install
modes.intent: Improve the platform itself: edit agent-platform code, shared rules, tools, tests, project dashboards, validation harnesses, or generated navigation.
audience: agent improving platform code or rules
developer adding tools, skills, validators, integrations, or dashboards
dependency_policy: Use editable Python installs for platform code when a virtual environment is used.
Install Node dependencies from lock files for projects being changed.
Include devDependencies and browser/test harnesses only for projects that need improvement or verification.
Run targeted and governance checks before close-out.
allowed_actions: run unit, browser, governance, and workspace health checks
update dependency manifests when installation workflow and audit records are followed
regenerate maps, boards, and static artifacts
must_not: install global dependencies without explicit justification and rollback path
mix unrelated project installs into one audit record
use developer install just to view existing artifacts

commands.purpose: Install the Python platform CLI in editable mode for source changes.
commands.command: cd agent-platform && python3 -m venv .venv && . .venv/bin/activate && python -m pip install -e .
commands.notes: Editable install keeps source changes live without reinstalling unless metadata changes.

commands.purpose: Run platform unit tests after source or config changes.
commands.command: cd agent-platform && PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m unittest discover -s tests
commands.notes: The current tests use the Python standard library unittest runner.

commands.purpose: Install monitor dependencies for development and verification.
commands.command: cd workspace-monitor && npm ci && npm test && npm run check && npm run build
commands.notes: Includes devDependencies needed for TypeScript checks and tests.

commands.purpose: Install and run browser validation when improving presentation artifacts or harnesses.
commands.command: cd presentation-agent && npm ci && npm run test:browser
commands.notes: Requires Playwright browser dependencies already recorded in the installation registry.

commands.purpose: Run shared governance checks after platform improvements.
commands.notes: Use with targeted checks for changed projects.

verification: agent-platform unit tests pass for changed Python code
workspace-monitor tests/check/build pass when monitor code changes
presentation-agent browser tests pass when presentation harness or HTML output changes
workspace health governance category passes before closing platform-level changes

selection_rules: If the user says use, run, view, deploy, browse, or try the platform, start from install_mode=user.
If the user says improve, develop, refactor, add a tool, add a skill, change platform behavior, or modify validators, use install_mode=developer.
If both are needed, do developer install in the owning project and document which user-facing install path remains valid.
If installing dependencies is not actually necessary for the requested task, do not run install commands; document the selected install mode only when it changes decisions.
If an install command is actually executed, follow _ops/workflows/58-installation-record.md before close-out.
